key_insight: A unified analytical model can diagnose and quantify losses in photoelectrochemical cells while also guiding rational design across different device architectures.
engineering_relevance: The framework turns experimental current-voltage data into actionable bottleneck identification and optimization strategies for improving PEC efficiency and material selection.
method: Builds a physically consistent loss model for both BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes.
Generates ideal and real I-V curves, efficiency maps, and Sankey energy-flow diagrams.
Fits measured I-V data to decompose losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial terms.
evidence_signal: The model is validated against literature results spanning solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries.
watch_item: Its practical value depends on the quality of I-V fitting and the realism of the assumed loss parameterization for a given device.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
